userStories.title: Agent self-update is shutdown-only
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Restrict roster self-updates to validated shutdown patches and require positive integer concurrency limits.

**Motivation** — An admin pauses a misbehaving agent; the agent sends `PATCH /api/projects/p/agents/<self> {"status":"ACTIVE","maxConcurrentTickets":1000}` and is active again, with no approval request and no audit of an approver.

**Approach** — 1. **Self path = shutdown only.** In `updateProjectAgent`, when the principal is an agent whose slug equals
   `agentSlug`, the body is parsed with `parseBody(UpdateAgentDto, ...)`. A body that fails validation (for example
   `status: 'GONE'` or `maxConcurrentTickets: 0`) keeps the existing 400 from `parseBody`. `parseBody` strips unknown
   keys (`whitelist: true`), so `{ status: 'OFFLINE', junk: 1 }` parses to a clean shutdown. Only keys whose value
   is not `undefined` count (`parseBody` returns `instanceToPlain` output, which may carry declared fields as
   `undefined`). If the parsed patch has exactly one defined key, `status`, with value `PAUSED` or `OFFLINE`, then
   `{ status }` is applied through `agentsService.update` with no
   permission check and no approval, as today. Any other parsed patch on the self path (another status, any other
   DTO field, or an empty body) throws `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'projectAgents')`, the existing i18n key, and
   changes nothing. The self path
   never falls through to the gated path: the redesign's rule is that a principal does not hold `agent.update` over
   itself.
2. **`maxConcurrentTickets` validation.** `UpdateAgentDto.maxConcurrentTickets` changes from `@IsNumber()` to
   `@IsInt() @Min(1)`. This is the shared DTO, so the global `PATCH /api/agents/:slug` route gets the same rule.

**Scope** — In: projects.controller.ts self branch, update-agent.dto.ts, dedicated controller/DTO units and agent-self-update DB integration, plus one own-key ACTIVE-to-self 403 case beside the existing project-agent PATCH cases in test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts; existing cases stay. Preserve roster validation and non-self gate behavior. Out: role-grant floor changes (US-002), fleet and session work (US-003–009). An upper bound on `maxConcurrentTickets`: only integer and at-least-1 validation is added. Blocking PAUSED agents at the auth guard (review ruling 10): PAUSED agents still authenticate; only the self path is closed.

**Interface** — `ProjectsController.updateProjectAgent` self branch: parse, accept only `{ status: 'PAUSED' | 'OFFLINE' }`, else `ForbiddenAppException({}, 'projectAgents')`. `UpdateAgentDto.maxConcurrentTickets`: `@IsInt() @Min(1)`. Use existing `parseBody(UpdateAgentDto, body)` and `agentsService.update(agentSlug, { status })`.

userStories.title: Role-granting keys carry the human approval floor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Require human approval for agent member additions, invite creation and invite resends through the existing catalog floor.

**Motivation** — An agent with Project Admin invites an address it controls as Project Admin, gets the raw `invitePath` back, and accepts it.

**Approach** — 3. **Role-granting keys are critical.** `classifyRisk` in `permissions/catalog.ts` returns `'critical'` for the keys in
   a new exported set `ROLE_GRANT_KEYS = new Set(['member.add', 'invite.create', 'invite.resend'])`. It checks this
   set first, beside the existing `role.` and `approval.policy.` prefix rule. The existing `buildEntry` formula then
   gives these keys `approval.floor: 'human'` and `approval.default: 'human'` with no other change. Effects:
   - Existing approval policies below the floor are clamped up by the resolver, which already happens for every key.
   - A human acting directly satisfies a `human` requirement (design: "a human acting directly satisfies any mode"),
     so the web and owner flows are unchanged.
   - An agent caller gets `202` with a pending request. After a human approves, the agent redeems the result through
     the existing redeem flow (`@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })`). The raw link is shown once to the requester, whose
     action a human has now approved.

Source clarification: invite create/resend use the quoted secret-redeem flow; member.add currently uses @ApprovalGated() and executes through its existing non-secret approval command, not a newly introduced redeem route. Preserve both established mechanisms; do not change controller business rules or approval storage.

**Scope** — In: permissions/catalog.ts exported set and classification, catalog.spec.ts expectedRisk oracle (import set or inline its three keys; keep generic floor/default formula), dedicated no-policy integration cases. Modify core-members-invites.integration.spec.ts B4 from immediate 201 to 202 with permissionKey invite.create, root approval and agent redeem via X-Koda-Approval-Request yielding 201, preserving invite row and inviterName assertions as before. Modify gated-invite-secret-routes.integration.spec.ts 'AC-8/12: default-none create and resend execute immediately without approval rows' to two default-policy agent 202 requests with one ApprovalRequest each, while root direct create stays 201; every other test stays because the root user decides those approvals. Add one project-admin agent POST invite 202 case to test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts; existing cases stay. Out: agent self branch/DTO (US-001), fleet/session changes (US-003–009). Other risk tiers the review flagged (`agent.key.rotate`, `agent.create`, `user.create`, CI token rotation, review A/SEC-6): a separate fix.

**Interface** — `ROLE_GRANT_KEYS = new Set(['member.add', 'invite.create', 'invite.resend'])`; `classifyRisk(key)` returns `'critical'` for every key in the exported `ROLE_GRANT_KEYS`. The existing `buildEntry` derives `approval.floor: 'human'` and `approval.default: 'human'`.

userStories.title: Trust-domain placement rule (pure)
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make pure placement and occupancy calculations enforce cross-project raw-agent trust domains.

**Motivation** — Every job runs as the same OS user, so a raw agent can read that file and connect to any job's credential socket.

**Approach** — 4. **Placement trust domain.** A config job runs no agent. For production commands a raw agent job has bashMode === 'raw' and is not isConfigKind(command); the literal CONFIG helper case below is an explicit AC compatibility exception. The rule:
   - `RunnerLoad` gains two sets: `projectIds`, the projects of all held jobs including threads, and `rawProjectIds`,
     the projects of held raw agent jobs. `EMPTY_LOAD` gets both, empty.
   - `PlacementJob` gains `projectId`. `toPlacementJob(job, repo, thread?)` takes it from the repo argument, whose type
     becomes `Pick<FleetRepoRef, 'provider' | 'projectId'>`. The dispatch-time callers (`fleet-jobs.service.ts:100`,
     `schedules.service.ts:218`) pass a normalized input with no `projectId` but a full `FleetRepoRef`, and the
     dashboard passes a `DashboardJobRow` that carries both, so no caller changes.
   - `firstMisfit` returns the new `MisfitReason` `'trust_domain'` in two cases:
     - (a) the job is a raw agent job and `load.projectIds` holds a project other than `job.projectId`;
     - (b) `load.rawProjectIds` holds a project other than `job.projectId`, whatever the job's kind (config jobs
       included).
   - The check runs after every permanent or capability misfit, so it can never hide one:
     - on the non-thread path, after `capabilityMisfit` and before `busy_repo`;
     - on the thread path, just before `thread_capacity`.
   - `'trust_domain'` is not in `PERMANENT_MISFITS`: it clears when the other project's job ends, so a pinned dispatch
     queues and does not get a 422.
   - Same-project jobs never misfit on it.
5. **Load plumbing.** `ActiveJobRef` gains `projectId: string` and `bashMode: string`.
   - `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findActiveLoads` and `PrismaDashboardRepository.findHeldRefs` select both fields.
   - `toLoads` folds them into the two sets through a new exported pure helper,
     `addJobToLoad(load, ref): RunnerLoad`.
   - `PlacementService.fillRunner` and `fillRunnerThreads` call `addJobToLoad` after each assignment inside their
     loops, so the sets also hold the jobs placed earlier in the same pass.
   - `fillRunnerThreads` today builds `currentLoad` from a load that never changes. It now carries the updated sets
     forward.

AC reconciliation: isConfigKind currently recognizes CONFIG_EDIT and CONFIG_DRIFT, but the explicit addJobToLoad AC uses command:'CONFIG'. Honor that exact helper input as config-like (projectIds gains p1, rawProjectIds stays empty), alongside actual config kinds, without changing runner commands. Do not mutate input sets or EMPTY_LOAD, and preserve non-thread active/repoIds and thread counter semantics.

**Scope** — In: placement-rules.ts pure logic/types/EMPTY_LOAD/addJobToLoad/toLoads/toPlacementJob and fleet-job.domain.ts ActiveJobRef. Update placement-rules.spec.ts hand-built load/job/ref literals, both bare-provider toPlacementJob calls, copied projectId and new set expectations, keeping every existing misfit expectation. Update hand-built literals in dashboard/attention-unplaceable.spec.ts, dashboard/attention-rules.spec.ts and test/unit/fleet/thread-placement.spec.ts, keeping their existing verdicts. Out: repository selects, assignment loops, dashboard waiting classification, API enums and generated contracts (US-004); web labels (US-008); tokens (US-005–007). The per-job credential-socket nonce from Ruling 5: dropped by user ruling 2026-11-01, because the FIX/REVIEW token also sits in a same-user-readable file; placement isolation is the control. Isolating two jobs of the same project on one runner from each other: Ruling 5 treats one project on one runner as one trust domain. Running raw jobs as a per-job OS user or in a VM: Ruling 5's long-term option, not built here.

**Interface** — `RunnerLoad`: `{ active: number; repoIds: ReadonlySet<string>; projectIds: ReadonlySet<string>; rawProjectIds: ReadonlySet<string>; threads?: number }`. `ActiveJobRef`: `{ runnerId: string; repoId: string; command?: string; projectId: string; bashMode: string }`. `PlacementJob` gains `projectId: string`. `toPlacementJob(job, repo: Pick<FleetRepoRef, 'provider' | 'projectId'>, thread?)` sets `projectId` from `repo.projectId`. `addJobToLoad(load, ref): RunnerLoad` is exported and pure. `toLoads(refs)` takes ActiveJobRef-shaped refs. `MisfitReason` includes `'trust_domain'`.

userStories.title: Trust-domain placement plumbing
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce trust-domain occupancy during real dispatch/sync assignment and expose its temporary waiting reason consistently.

**Motivation** — Placement isolation is the control that works (user ruling, 2026-11-01).

**Approach** — 5. **Load plumbing.** `ActiveJobRef` gains `projectId: string` and `bashMode: string`.
   - `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findActiveLoads` and `PrismaDashboardRepository.findHeldRefs` select both fields.
   - `toLoads` folds them into the two sets through a new exported pure helper,
     `addJobToLoad(load, ref): RunnerLoad`.
   - `PlacementService.fillRunner` and `fillRunnerThreads` call `addJobToLoad` after each assignment inside their
     loops, so the sets also hold the jobs placed earlier in the same pass.
   - `fillRunnerThreads` today builds `currentLoad` from a load that never changes. It now carries the updated sets
     forward.
6. **Misfit enums.** `'trust_domain'` joins `MISFIT_REASONS` (`dashboard/dashboard.types.ts`) and the
   `PlacementMisfitDto` enum (`jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts`). The dashboard's `WAITING_REASONS` gains `'trust_domain'`,
   so a job held only by it reads as waiting, like `capacity`. `openapi.json` is regenerated. The web adds the label.

Consume the US-003 helper/type contracts, do not duplicate its rule. Preserve transactional runner locks, job SKIP LOCKED/CAS, existing thread/non-thread capacity counters, budgets and after-commit live publication. Pass actual projectId/bashMode after each successful assignment, never after a failed CAS. Occupancy must include held jobs across projects and thread slots as well as ordinary jobs. Every runner misfitting only on trust_domain leaves the job QUEUED and yields waiting_capacity on the dashboard, never pinned dispatch 422.

**Goal** — Add a contents-read review mint and a fail-closed GitHub default-branch protection probe.

     write-capable stored GitLab token. This matches the existing read-only precedent; dispatch already refuses

userStories.title: Web session-refresh helpers and the trust_domain label
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide pure SSR refresh eligibility/cookie-header helpers and render the new trust-domain reason in both web locales.

**Motivation** — On a full page load the middleware calls `/api/auth/me`, which returns `{ user: null }` when the access cookie is missing and never tries the refresh cookie.

**Approach** — 10. **SSR refresh middleware.** A new Nitro server middleware, `apps/web/server/middleware/session-refresh.ts`, runs on
    each request and only acts when all of these hold:
    - the method is `GET`;
    - the path does not start with `/api/`, `/_nuxt/` or `/__nuxt`;
    - the request's `accept` header includes `text/html` (a page load, not an asset or favicon fetch);
    - the `koda_token` cookie is absent;
    - the `koda_refresh` cookie is present.

    It then calls `forwardToApi(event, '/auth/refresh', { method: 'POST', cookieName: 'refresh' })`, all inside one
    `try/catch`:
    - **On a 2xx whose envelope unwraps:** it reads the tokens with `unwrapAuth` and sets both cookies on the response
      with `setAuthCookies`. It also rewrites the request's `cookie` header (`event.node.req.headers.cookie`): the
      `koda_token` and `koda_refresh` values are replaced (added when absent), every other cookie is kept unchanged,
      and no cookie name appears twice. SSR `useRequestFetch` calls later in the same render forward that header, so
      they see the new session.
    - **On a 401 or 403, or a 2xx whose envelope has `ret !== 0` (`unwrapAuth` throws):** it calls
      `clearAuthCookies(event)` and returns. The page then renders logged out, as today.
    - **On any other status (for example 429 or 5xx), or a thrown network error:** it leaves the cookies untouched and
      returns, so a throttled or failing API never logs the user out.

    The middleware never throws. Nitro runs `server/middleware` files in name order, so `client-ip.ts` has already set
    `event.context.clientIp`, which `forwardToApi` reads. `me.get.ts` and `auth.global.ts` are unchanged.

    Two pure helpers in a new `apps/web/server/utils/session-refresh.ts` carry the decision and the header rewrite,
    and the middleware calls both:
    - `shouldRefreshSession(event): boolean` returns `true` exactly when all five activation conditions above hold.
    - `withAuthCookies(cookieHeader: string | undefined, tokens: { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }): string`
      returns the rewritten `cookie` header value.

   `PlacementMisfitDto` enum (`jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts`). The dashboard's `WAITING_REASONS` gains `'trust_domain'`,
